quest.title: The Law of Boundaries
quest.description: Sucrose is working on a new alchemical potion, but no matter how she tweaks the formula, it never comes out right...
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Freedom x3, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Go to the Crafting Bench in Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm... Given previous results, I should make a few adjustments to the experiment, and ensure that the materials and equipment are all in order...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #As for the potion I need to make... Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to help with your "task." We wanted to see if you could use some extra hands...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: My "task"... Oh, you mean the one Mr. Albedo told me about? The one from the Hexenzirkel?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Well, you're just in time. The experiment is ongoing, and I was just about to work on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ongoing? So, you've been working on it all this time?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes. It aligns with other research topics I've been working on, so it hasn't been too much extra work.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Still...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Is there a problem with the experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I've been "unsuccessful" so far.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so it keeps failing, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's not as simple as just "failing." The whole theoretical framework behind this task is a bit more complicated than I imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what's this task exactly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right! You still haven't told us what kind of experiment it is.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: One meant to develop a potion that can transform Sweet Flowers into a variant 16 times its normal size.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That is to say, the formulation of "Botanical Augmentation Reagent Type IV, Iteration VII" — as you can probably guess, this is my seventh time running the experiment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! So, basically, we need to make growth serum! Or, the seventh version of one.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: W—Well, yeah... That's about right.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: This is my seventh attempt, but I didn't make many adjustments to the formula this time, because both the theoretical principles behind this experiment and the products of the process prove there's nothing wrong with it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you haven't "succeeded" yet, right?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes. I'm thinking that it's not my current formula that is wrong, per se, but rather... Some other key element is missing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh... Hehe, then Paimon knows just what to do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We came here to do just that, after all!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Um, we could try, it's just... I would need to adjust the ratios in the original formula, and that might make the potion even more unstable...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, we are NOT trying that! Just show us the original!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: That said, I'm still missing two ingredients.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that we can help with. What do we need to get?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I need spring water from Springvale to use as the base, as well as Eye of the Storm fragments... But, that last one could be tricky.

choices.text: Perhaps we could try adding a little essence of Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, well that's why we're helping ou— Wait a second, Paimon is NOT an ingredient!

talks.objective: Defeat the Eye of the Storm

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me look at the formula again...

talks.objective: Go to the Crafting Bench in Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Alright, the ingredients are ready, and the cauldron is just over there, so we should be good to go. But, um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No, no. It's just... Do you mind if I watch from the side? Just for the purposes of accurate recording, I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I know lots of people don't like being scrutinized during experiments, so...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's no problem at all.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Thanks. Then, I'm ready to go whenever you are. I'll make sure to take detailed notes, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So, are you ready to start the experiment?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: #...Ready to start the experiment, {NICKNAME}? Don't worry, I'll document everything.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That's it... Your execution was perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes, I don't see any flaws in the brewing at all... Let me extract some and test the product's composition. One moment...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sucrose extracts some of the potion and uses a device to examine its composition...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes, like I said — flawless execution. The potion is perfect. It's exactly what I was expecting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, was the seventh time the charm?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Upon examination, it seems identical to the previous six iterations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Wouldn't that make the results identical?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. Experimental outcomes can differ even with similar variables all around. You never know what the result will be — that's what makes experiments valuable in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Come, let's test this thing out. I planted some Sweet Flowers beforehand which we can use.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: We just need to douse them with the potion and see what happens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we poured the growth serum on the flowers... Is that all we need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yep. The flowers need to fully absorb the potion, so it might take some time before we see a reaction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happens then?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The flowers will grow in size while maintaining their original appearance. But then, when they reach 12 to 14 times their normal size, this will prove more than they can bear...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: As if some upper limit has been reached, they will wither and rot, assuming unnatural forms until nothing is left of them but liquid.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what? So there's a problem with the growth serum, then!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No. I've adjusted the formula time and again, resolving all kinds of issues that arise when inducing small plants to grow larger.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Issues like... ensuring that the leaves don't get too large, strengthening root diameter and load-bearing capacity, calculating how the increase in surface area might affect sunlight exposure and nutrition...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why isn't it working, then?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Because the flowers cannot transcend... "As above, so below" is one of alchemy's guiding principles. Alchemy seeks mastery over matter, but this world has its limits.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's like... a "specification" etched into the law that governs all things. Part of the purpose of doing multiple experiments is to determine if this "specification" is stable.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, "failure" is also a viable result...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Exactly. It proves that the limit "continues to exist."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, this is all a bit over Paimon's head, but basically... You needed the experiment to fail to prove that the limits and borders in this world are stable?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a weird experiment... Huh? Looks like one of the flowers is reacting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second... That's not a Sweet Flower at all!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Careful! I—It's a Whopperflower! It must have absorbed some of the potion. Wait. But that's happened before, and it's never gotten this big, either. Can this mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can talk about this later. Let's get rid of it first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we did it. Even at that size, a Whopperflower is just a Whopperflower.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: ...Hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, uh... was it supposed to get that big?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I could only make a rough estimate during the battle, but it looked at least... 16 times its original size, maybe even larger.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: This means that the experiment... worked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but isn't that a good thing?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I'm still not sure what the implications are... But if further attempts succeed in reproducing this result...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That means that something's different... Perhaps the limits and laws of this world are changing due to some unknown factor...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I can't say if that's good or bad, but from an alchemical perspective at least, expanded boundaries means that more possibilities are now open to us.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Either way, this brings my task to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems so...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hmm. That said, it could also be an effect of the person who made the potion. There could also have been something special about this particular Whopperflower...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: There's a lot that still needs to be confirmed, so I suppose this task opens the way for further questions...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we're here if you ever need some help!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could we try using that growth serum on Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, just think about it... Paimon could probably beat a whole gang of Treasure Hoarders to a pulp if she were 16 times bigger!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I have my doubts. The only reason the serum worked on the Whopperflower was because its internal structure was similar enough to a Sweet Flower... If you drank some...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: You might become 16 times bigger, but you might also turn into a plant-based lifeform.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, nope. That's not happening, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, Paimon wanted to ask... Why is all your research focused on things like Sweet Flowers and Sunsettias?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh, that's simple. Both Sunsettias and Sweet Flower nectar taste sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So, in that sense, accidentally making a Whopperflower 16 times bigger comes with a hidden benefit, because Whopperflower Nectar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Tastes exactly like Sweet Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: That's right! Once I've extracted the sugar from the nectar, I'll give you some.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you got it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep, let's go.
